name: St Duje's Cathedral
blurb: Former Diocletian mausoleum turned cathedral, mixing Roman temple and church styles; the bell tower gives wide city views.

name: Diocletian's Palace basement
blurb: Well-preserved palace substructure, now a museum and a Game of Thrones location; a guide helps because the halls are sparse.

name: Archaeological Museum
blurb: Croatia's oldest museum (1820), with Roman finds from the colonies Salona and Narona; most labels are in Croatian only.
priceText: Adults €8; children, pupils, students, pensioners €4 (needs a Croatian-issued document); free on Mondays
when: Jun–Sep: Mon–Sat 09:00–14:00 and 15:00–20:00; closed Sun; winter hours not shown

name: Temple of Jupiter (baptistery)
blurb: Ancient Roman temple later turned into a baptistery beside the cathedral; a quick, cheap stop.

name: Pazar farmers market
blurb: Farmers market with fresh fruit, vegetables and more; Saturday and Sunday mornings are the best time to go.
when: Best on Sat and Sun mornings

name: Kod Joze konoba
blurb: Family-run traditional konoba serving tasty dishes; prices are very reasonable for the quality and atmosphere.

name: St Riva bar
blurb: Bar with an upper floor overlooking the promenade; a handy stop for a cheap evening drink.

name: Sanctuary Bar
blurb: Craft cocktail bar with a selection of craft beers, open from 09:00 until midnight.

name: Marjan hill walk
blurb: Green hill west of the centre for walks, jogging and biking; the Telegrin peak (178 m) gives a wide view over Split.

name: Fort Lovrijenac
blurb: Fortress on a 37 m rock outside the western walls, built to guard against land and sea attacks; free with the City Walls ticket.
priceText: €15, or free with City Walls ticket

name: Dubrovnik Cathedral (Assumption)
blurb: Baroque cathedral whose first church was reportedly paid for by Richard the Lionheart after a shipwreck on his way home.

name: Maritime Museum
blurb: One of the city's most important museums, on how sailing and shipbuilding built the Dubrovnik Republic.

name: Sponza Palace
blurb: Gothic-Renaissance palace that survived the 1667 earthquake; it houses historic archives and a memorial room for the defenders.

name: Barba
blurb: Sea street food with big portions and friendly staff; take it away or eat on the steps in the Old Town.

name: Pizzeria La Luna
blurb: Large, good-value pizzas with fresh ingredients; only pizza is served before 17:00, and service can be slow.

name: Culture Club Revelin
blurb: Club playing techno and other styles, open nightly from 23:00 until 06:00.

name: Beer Factory
blurb: Courtyard bar that is among the cheapest places for a beer in the Old Town, with reasonably priced snacks.

name: Dubrovnik Aquarium
blurb: Small aquarium open daily until 21:00; at €4 it is one of the cheapest paid stops in the city.

name: Ljubljana Castle
blurb: Hilltop castle whose tower has wide views over the city to the Kamnik Alps; the courtyard and chapel are free to enter.
priceText: Castle ticket incl. tower: adults €19.00 at counter, €17.10 online; children 7–18, students, pensioners €13.50 at counter, €12.15 online; courtyard free (Wikivoyage)
when: Hours not on official site; last ticket 1 hour before closing

name: MG+ Museum of Modern Art
blurb: Holds the national collection of 20th-century Slovene art, from paintings to video; a strong pick for contemporary art fans.

name: Plečnik House
blurb: Home of architect Jože Plečnik from 1921 to 1957, with his original furniture, sketches and plans on view.

name: University Botanic Garden Ljubljana
blurb: Founded in 1810 as a garden of native flora; the tropical glasshouse makes a warm escape in winter.

name: Central Market
blurb: Open-air market with seasonal local produce, plus cheeses, breads and meats in the building next door.

name: Gostilna Sokol
blurb: Traditional Slovene restaurant where staff wear folk costume; touristy, but big portions and good value for money.

name: Metelkova mesto
blurb: Alternative squat with six clubs, each with its own music; Gala Hala is the biggest, with everything from funk to rap.

name: Pod Skalco
blurb: Pub with an almost 150-year tradition, mostly used by locals; loud music, open until 03:00 every night.

name: Water City of Atlantis
blurb: Water park with 14 pools, thermal baths, slides and saunas; a warm option on a chilly December day.
when: Hours not confirmed; Adventure World closed for renovation until about 24 Oct 2026 (official site)

name: Bunk'Art 1
blurb: Cold War bunker turned history and contemporary-art museum, with almost 3,000 m² of space on several underground floors.

name: House of Leaves
blurb: 1930s building that began as Albania's first maternity hospital and later became an interrogation and surveillance centre.

name: Et'hem Bey Mosque
blurb: One of Albania's most beautiful mosques, finished in 1821 after about 28 years of building; reopened in 2021 after restoration.

name: Studio House Kadare
blurb: Former home and workplace of novelist Ismail Kadare (1974–89) in a 1972 modernist building; the student ticket is just 80 lek.
priceText: Adult 500 lek, family (2+) 250 lek, student 80 lek

name: Oda restaurant
blurb: Traditional Albanian cooking in an old Tirana house; this is the original Oda, not the rival Oda Garden south of the Pazari.

name: Flower's
blurb: Budget daily-menu spot where free water and bread come with the meal; try the creamy eggplant dish muzaka.

name: Tunel
blurb: Bar and club with sometimes international DJs; rooftop in summer, basement in winter, and it closes around 02:00 or 03:00.
when: Winter in the basement; latest close 02:00–03:00

name: Komiteti Kafe Muzeum
blurb: Bohemian café-bar packed with communist-era relics and farm tools; a quirky stop for an evening drink.

name: Dajti Express cable car
blurb: Austrian-built cable car that takes about 15 minutes up Mount Dajti; locals go there to escape the city and eat spit-roast lamb.
when: Mon & Wed–Fri 09:00–18:30; Sat–Sun 09:00–19:00; closed Tue (official site)

name: Brar Canyon and Bridge
blurb: Panoramic canyon with an Ottoman bridge, a waterfall and a cave near Shëngjergj village, close to the capital.

name: Sebilj fountain
blurb: Wooden, Ottoman-style fountain in the middle of Baščaršija square; built in 1753 and moved to its current spot in 1891.

name: Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque
blurb: Ottoman mosque from around 1530 in the Old Town heart; visitors welcome if they dress appropriately and respect prayer times.

name: Tunnel of Hope
blurb: Tunnel dug under the airport runway, a lifeline during the 1990s siege; a sobering stop for understanding the war.
priceText: 15 KM; 5 KM for students; audio guide extra

name: War Childhood Museum
blurb: Personal belongings and stories of childhood during the siege of Sarajevo, with an audio guide that explains each item.

name: Markale Market
blurb: Market hall opened in 1895 with local meat, cheese and vegetable sellers; walnuts are a speciality here.

name: Petica Ferhatović
blurb: Spacious, popular spot for fresh beef ćevapi; the waitresses wear traditional Bosnian dress.

name: Café de Paris
blurb: Riverside bar with outdoor seating, craft beers from Sarajevo microbreweries and local rakija; try the quince one.

name: Tre Bicchieri Wine Store & Tasting Bar
blurb: Cosy wine bar with a long list of Italian wines, good music and a relaxed atmosphere.

name: Ilidža Thermal Riviera
blurb: Indoor and outdoor pools fed by sulphur-rich thermal water, plus a wave pool, slides and sauna; a bit dated but relaxing.
priceText: Basic entry 9 KM; extra for wellness and fitness centres

name: Dariva Canyon promenade
blurb: Eight-kilometre pedestrian promenade from the old town along the Miljacka canyon to Goat's Bridge; scenic and free.

name: Stone Bridge
blurb: Twelve-arch stone bridge over the Vardar, a symbol of Skopje since the 15th century; the pedestrian bridge is 214 m long.

name: Mustafa Pasha Mosque
blurb: Intact 1492 mosque on a plateau above the Old Bazaar, rated among the finest Islamic buildings in the country.

name: Mother Teresa Memorial House
blurb: Tranquil modern chapel marking Mother Teresa's Skopje roots; she lived in the city until she was 18, and entry is free.
when: New hours announced for July, check; Wikivoyage: Mon–Fri 09:00–20:00, Sat–Sun 09:00–14:00

name: Skopje Fortress
blurb: Fortress on the highest hill in the Skopje valley, with wide city views; its oldest walls use huge stone blocks.

name: Bit Pazar
blurb: Big food market where the Old Bazaar ends; fresh produce, cheese, teas and spices on a site used for hundreds of years.

name: Restaurant Old House
blurb: Wood-and-stone house from 1836, a protected monument and considered Macedonia's oldest traditional house still in use.

name: Irish Pub St Patrick
blurb: Classic Irish pub open until midnight on most nights and until 01:00 on Friday and Saturday.

name: Rock Bar Krug
blurb: Genuine neighbourhood rock bar rather than a touristy nightlife spot; a good look at how locals go out.

name: Skopje Walks
blurb: Free walking tour of Centar and the Old Town, about three hours and leaving daily at 10:00; tips are expected.

name: Millennium Cross Cable Car
blurb: Cable car from Middle Vodno up to the Millennium Cross, opened in 2011; a quick way to the top of Vodno mountain.

name: St John's Co-Cathedral
blurb: Ornate knights' church with a chapel for each 'langue' and Caravaggio's Beheading of St John inside.
priceText: €15 adults (includes audio guide); buy online to skip the queue
when: Mon–Sat 09:00–16:45 (last entry 16:15); closed Sun and holidays

name: Palace of the Grand Masters (Armoury)
blurb: Former Grand Masters' palace, now the seat of Malta's president and parliament; staterooms when open, plus the knights' armoury.
when: Mar–Dec 10:00–18:00; Jan–Feb 09:00–17:00 (armoury sometimes closed for functions)

name: Fort St Elmo (National War Museum)
blurb: Fort at the tip of the peninsula, built after the 1551 Dragut raid and key in the 1565 Great Siege; now the war museum.

name: Saluting Battery
blurb: Valletta gun battery where a salute is fired at noon and 16:00 Monday to Saturday; a cheap, quick stop.

name: Museum Cafe
blurb: Cosy old-style Maltese café with an impressive interior and original ftira (ring bread); the owner is very welcoming.

name: Rubino
blurb: Maltese restaurant open since 1906 serving traditional cooking; reservations are recommended.

name: Cafe Society
blurb: Queer bar in Valletta with good drinks, open daily until 01:00; the crowd often spills onto the street in warmer months.

name: The Pub
blurb: Valletta pub where actor Oliver Reed died after a drinking match against a group of sailors.

name: Coastal Walk
blurb: Walk along the sea walls around Valletta; from the ferry landing you can scramble over rocks towards the peninsula's tip.

name: Malta Experience
blurb: Hourly audiovisual show with a quick overview of Malta's history, useful before you visit the sites.

name: Church of St Lazarus
blurb: Ninth-century Orthodox church, reputedly built around the tomb of the biblical Lazarus, brother of Mary.

name: Hala Sultan Tekke
blurb: Mosque said to be the tomb of Umm Haram, foster mother of the Prophet Muhammad.

name: Larnaca Salt Lake
blurb: Flocks of pink flamingos gather on the salt lake from November to March, making it a winter highlight.

name: Thalassa Municipal Museum
blurb: Ayia Napa's municipal museum of fossils, archaeology and marine life, with a replica of the Hellenistic trade ship Kyrenia II.
when: Mon & Sat 09:00–14:00; Tue–Fri 09:00–17:00; Sun closed; same hours in summer and winter (official site)

name: Militzis
blurb: Long-running favourite for honest Cypriot food with its own house wine; no frills, and often packed.

name: Edesma Cyprus Taverna
blurb: Authentic Cypriot taverna whose dishes are seasoned with white wine and homemade zivania; halloumi and feta salads are good.

name: Savino
blurb: Lively rock bar with lots of seats, often a good crowd and live music now and then.

name: Blue Pine Bar
blurb: Dimly lit wood-decor bar with a large spirits range and blues memorabilia; it gets busy after dark.

name: Windsurf City
blurb: Windsurfing, foil and paddleboard lessons with friendly staff; check whether they run in December before you plan a session.

name: Sea caves near Cape Greco
blurb: Sea caves under a cliff in a small bay near Cape Greco, reached on foot or by road, with boat trips on offer.
